D010_m001.question:
It’s a bit hard to put into words because it feels like I’ve been two different people this past year.

About seven months ago, for roughly two months, I was “on fire,” is how I kept describing it. At school I was buzzing—pacing up and down the halls between classes, jumping into other teachers’ lessons, starting clubs, rewriting curriculums at 2 a.m. I couldn’t sit still in staff meetings; my legs were going, my hands tapping nonstop. I talked constantly—my students joked they couldn’t get a word in. My wife kept asking me to slow down, but I felt like everyone else was just too slow.

I was also getting unusually angry over small things—kids whispering, someone being late—and I snapped a few times in ways that embarrassed me. I started to feel like I had some “special calling,” like I was meant to revolutionize education nationwide, that important people would notice me. Around that time I kept smelling smoke or this strange chemical odor when no one else did. I even did some really out-of-character stuff sexually—flirting with a colleague, sexting a former student’s parent. I knew it was wrong, but it felt almost impossible to stop.

After that, it’s like someone pulled the plug. For about five months now, I’ve felt flat and empty—like I’m just going through the motions. I barely talk in the teachers’ lounge. I avoid friends, let calls go to voicemail, even dodge family dinners. My wife says I’m “not there” even when I’m on the couch next to her.

I can’t decide anything—what to wear, what to cook, which assignment to give. I’ll stand in front of the closet or the fridge and just stare. I’m still showing up to class, but I feel disconnected from the kids, like I’m watching someone else teach. Everything that once felt urgent and meaningful now feels distant, and it’s really affecting my work and my marriage.
D010_m001.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010_m001.answer: D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010_m014.question:
For about a month now, I just haven’t felt like myself at all. It’s like I’m on this roller coaster that changes tracks every hour. One minute I’m buzzing, feeling on top of the world, convinced I can solve every open case in the lab, and the next I’m snapping at coworkers over tiny things or getting irrationally angry if someone questions me.

At work I’ve been taking on way too much—staying late, starting three or four analyses at once, reorganizing evidence logs at 3 a.m. because I “finally see the pattern.” My brain won’t slow down. Thoughts pile on top of each other so fast I lose my train of thought mid-sentence, then jump to something completely different.

What’s really scaring me is that I’m convinced people are watching me—like the lab cameras aren’t just for security, but someone’s monitoring me personally, maybe law enforcement or some higher agency. I’ve even started hearing voices, like a couple of distinct ones commenting on what I’m doing, saying things like “She knows too much” or “They’re coming.” This only started with this whole high-energy phase, and it’s gotten to the point where I’m not sleeping, barely eating, and I can’t function normally anymore.
D010_m014.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D010_m014.answer: B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

We finished a big project and everyone was congratulating me, and I felt nothing. Just empty. I go to work because I have to, but I walk around like I’m on autopilot. Sleep’s a mess. I fall asleep okay, but I keep waking up at 2 or 3 a.m., just staring at the ceiling for hours. Then about three weeks ago, everything flipped. I got this edge to me; the smallest thing on site sets me off. I’m yelling at guys for nothing. Sometimes I smell this strong perfume around me when no one’s there, like she’s nearby. It’s gotten to where the crew avoids me, and my boss pulled me aside because I’m too worked up to run things properly.

I don’t really know what’s going on with me, but the last couple of weeks have been… intense. It started maybe about two weeks ago. At first I just felt like I had so much energy. I’d close the café at 11 p.m., go home, and instead of crashing I’d stay up until 3 or 4 cleaning my room, reorganizing my closet, planning this online jewelry business. I’m only sleeping like three hours a night, but I don’t feel tired at all, almost wired.

Everyone keeps saying I’m “snappy.” Tiny things set me off—customers taking too long to order, my coworker messing up a latte. I’ll just blow up, then feel like it’s their fault for being slow or stupid.

I also went on this huge online shopping binge—clothes, gadgets, skin-care stuff—maxed out my credit card and borrowed from my mom, saying it was all “investments.”

What’s really freaking me out is my body. I’m convinced something’s seriously wrong inside, like my organs are rotting or infected, even though tests were fine. Sometimes I smell this awful, rotten smell, like garbage or something dead, even when no one else smells it. All of this has started to mess with my job and my family; they say I’m “not myself.”
